Large-scale emigration from Cape Verde, which began in the 19th century when New England whaling ships took on crews at Brava and Fogo, and grew with every drought and famine.

Cape Verdeans settled in Massachusetts and Rhode Island, working on whalers, in cranberry bogs and in mills. Under Portuguese rule thousands were also sent as contract workers to Sao Tome and Angola. In the 20th century many went to Portugal, the Netherlands and France. Today more Cape Verdeans and their descendants live abroad than on the islands, and money they send home is a large share of the economy. The longing for those who left is a main theme of morna. See also Mindelo and Portuguese rule.
